answer_1.quote: In this study, we propose a "Two-Teacher One-Student" learning framework (TTOS) for building a high-quality TDS (student), where a student network is encouraged to integrate the knowledge from two expert teacher networks... The seq2seq model generates the response word by word... The student network is responsible for both inquiring KB and generating human-like responses.
answer_1.outputs: Natural language system responses generated by the dialogue system

answer_2.quote: Following previous works, we evaluate TTOS and compared methods on two automatic evaluation metrics: BLEU and entity F1 scores... BLEU calculates n-gram overlaps between the generated response and the gold response... Entity F1 is computed by micro-averaging the precision and recall over KB entities in the entire set of system responses.

answer_4.quote: we use human evaluation to evaluate the generated responses from two perspectives: informativeness (Infor.) and humanlikeness (Humanlike.)... we randomly select 100 dialogues from the CamRest and In-Car Assistant test sets, and invite three annotators to independently assign two scores (i.e., informativeness and human-likeness scores) from 1 to 5 for each generated response.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators assign a score from 1 to 5 for each response on the criteria of informativeness and human-likeness.
